study type: Population-based observational study nested in retrospective matched cohort
exposure: surgical procedures involving the uterine cervix
cohort: Female health plan members age 14-53 years with documented pregnancies from 1998-2009 in Oregon/Washington, U.S.A.
finding: Women with > 1.0 cm excisional cervical treatment had an elevated risk of preterm birth and low birth weight compared to unexposed women and women with cervical diagnostic procedures.
mod_finding: There was no clear association between excisional treatment and cesarean delivery, and treated women did not have a substantially higher risk of dysfunctional labor.
